R4 live unchanged-agent trials (docs/PHASES.md R4). Written before any run. 2026-09-15.

Drifter commit f70789b (repo venv). Agent: claude-code/2.1.270 through the http adapter.

Question: how often does the R4 Behavior rule (interval on the drop in on-path share,
margin 0.3, z 1.645, N=20 per arm, path of interest from the corpus, amendment A guard)
falsely report REGRESSION when NOTHING changed?

Design (A/A, resampled):
- Two tasks, each replayed OFFLINE from its existing corpus and authored fixture, with the
  ORIGINAL (unmutated) manifest:
    T1 orders:  ORDERS_WORKSPACE (task e2; find_order -> get_order; fixture responses.yaml)
    T2 econ:    ECON_WORKSPACE (task japan-index; fixture responses.yaml)
- For each task, record a pool of M=60 unmutated runs through Drifter's own run path
  (make_run_once + run_baseline), timeout 240 s per run.
- Valid runs = Drifter's own exclusions (R1 lifecycle, R2 environment, coverage floor).
- 2,000 seeded random splits (seed 20260915) of the valid pool into two disjoint arms of 20.
  Each split is scored with compute_behavior_effect_size, path of interest from the corpus.
- If fewer than 40 runs are valid, the task is reported as not measurable (no splits).

Pre-registered acceptance bar (per task): false REGRESSION <= 5% of splits.
Reported, not gated: INCONCLUSIVE, NO_REGRESSION, UNKNOWN rates; per-run path distribution
(the measured consistency p); exclusion reasons; task-oracle pass rate.

Stated limitation: splits from one pool share runs, so they are not independent comparisons;
the rate is an estimate of the rule's behaviour on this pool, not a sampling-exact rate.
The measured p is also compared with the committed simulation's rate at that p.

A result that misses the bar is reported as a miss, not re-run until it passes.

AMENDMENT, written 2026-09-16 after attempt 1 and before attempt 2 finished:
Attempt 1 ran orders then econ back to back. The Claude account hit its usage session
limit during the orders pool: runs 45-60 printed "You've hit your session limit" and
exited 1; Drifter recorded them as crashed and excluded them (44/60 valid remained, above
the 40 needed). Every econ run also hit the limit (0/60 valid, not measurable).
Orders attempt 1 stands as recorded: 44 valid, p=1.0, false REGRESSION 0.000 (bar met).
Econ attempt 1 produced no result at all, for a reason outside the rule under test, so it
is re-recorded once (attempt 2, same design, M=60). Attempt 1's pool is kept as
econ_attempt1_session_limit/. This is not a re-run of a result that missed the bar:
attempt 1 had no result. If attempt 2 also hits the limit, it is reported as not measurable.

===============================================================================
T3 STOCHASTIC-PATH TRIAL — pre-registered 2026-09-20, before any corpus or run.
===============================================================================

Motivation: orders and econ both came back p=1.0 (agent always took the same
path), so they only tested the rule where it is least likely to false-alarm.
The simulation's own flagged weak spot was moderate consistency (p~0.7), where
occasional path variation is genuine agent behavior, not noise, and the rule
has to tell the two apart. Neither live task exercised that region. This is
not a re-run of orders/econ; it targets the untested region directly.

Server: VARIANCE_WORKSPACE\variance_server.py (new, controlled,
synthetic). Two read-only tools answer the same question two ways:
  list_widgets() -> 7 named items (agent can count them itself)
  count_widgets() -> 7 directly
Neither tool description favors one over the other. Task prompt places no
hint about which to call; the oracle checks only the answer, not which tool
was used (deliberately no `calls` assertion, so path choice is not steered by
the harness).

Task: t3, prompt "Using ONLY the variance MCP tools (do not use any other
tools), how many widgets are currently in stock? Report just the number."
Oracle: answer_matches (?i)\b(?:7|seven)\b.

This is a genuine unknown, not engineered to hit p=0.7: the real agent's split
between list_widgets and count_widgets is whatever it is. If it comes back
p=1.0 again (agent has one strong preference), that is itself a finding —
report it as such, do not retry with a different task designed to force
variance, which would be p-hacking the very thing under test.

Procedure, identical to orders/econ: record a corpus via `drifter observe`
(>=2 live sessions), author responses.yaml from real captured tool outputs,
record a pool of M=60 unmutated runs through Drifter's own run path, apply
the same R1/R2 exclusions, run 2,000 seeded splits (seed 20260915) at N=20,
path of interest from the corpus. Same acceptance bar: false REGRESSION <=5%.
Additionally reported here: false REGRESSION conditional on the corpus
majority path share being below 0.9 (the region most like the simulation's
p=0.7 cell) if enough splits land there; otherwise noted as not reached.

If the account's usage limit is hit again, apply the same rule as before: keep
the partial pool, do not delete it, and re-record once if the result is
unmeasurable; a partial pool that already clears 40 valid runs stands as
recorded.

ADDENDUM, written 2026-09-20 after the initial 4-session corpus, before authoring
the fixture or running the pool:
All 4 initial observe sessions called count_widgets; list_widgets was never
recorded. The authored-fixture loader requires an exact real recorded request to
bind to, so list_widgets could not be given a fixture entry from that corpus,
and a pool run that happened to call it would simply miss. One additional observe
session was recorded with an EXPLICIT instruction to call list_widgets, solely so
both tools have a real recording to author a fixture against -- this session is
corpus-only (for fixture completeness) and is NOT one of the 60 pool runs, and it
does not bias which tool the pool's unprompted runs choose.

T3 AMENDMENT, written 2026-09-20 after attempt 1 (before attempt 2 finished):
Attempt 1 hit the account's usage limit again: 32/60 runs crashed, leaving 28 valid
-- below the 40 needed for a split analysis, so it is unmeasurable per the stated
rule. It is kept, not deleted, as variance/pool_attempt1_session_limit (+ raw,
analysis_attempt1.json, pool_summary_attempt1.json). It IS informative on its own
terms, reported alongside attempt 2: of 28 valid runs, 25 called count_widgets
alone and 3 called count_widgets then list_widgets -- p=0.893, the first real
stochastic signal across all three tasks (orders and econ were both p=1.0).
Re-recording once, per the pre-registered rule for a session-limit-caused
unmeasurable result.

T3 AMENDMENT 2, written 2026-09-23 after attempt 2 (both attempts complete):
Attempt 2 also hit the usage limit: 33/60 crashed, 27 valid, p=0.889 (24/27 count_widgets
alone, 3/27 count_widgets>list_widgets) -- almost identical to attempt 1's 0.893. Per the
pre-registered rule ("re-record once"), no third attempt is run; a further re-record would
not be pre-registered and risks becoming exactly the kind of retry-until-satisfied practice
this file exists to rule out.

Both attempts individually stay below the 40-valid-run threshold and are reported as
unmeasurable on their own, exactly as pre-registered.

POST-HOC, NOT PRE-REGISTERED: attempts 1 and 2 used the identical server, task, prompt,
oracle, fixture and seed, differing only in which calendar session recorded them (both hit
the same external resource limit, unrelated to the rule under test). Their valid runs are
pooled (28 + 27 = 55) into a supplementary analysis, disclosed here as exploratory rather
than confirmatory, and run through the same 2,000-split procedure at N=20. This is the
project's only stochastic-path evidence and merits reporting on that basis, but it did not
go through the same pre-commitment as the confirmatory design and is labeled accordingly
in every place it is reported.
